snippet.title: HITMAN Villain Voice Actor Reacts to His Own Character | Experts React
snippet.description:
Philip Rosch, the actor behind Arthur Edwards, better known as The Constant, joins Gamology to react to cutscenes from the Hitman trilogy and revisit one of his favorite roles of his entire career. From The Constant’s measured walk and controlled voice to his tense confrontations with Diana Burnwood and Agent 47, Philip breaks down the acting choices behind the character.

Philip shares memories of his first motion capture shoot, explains why The Constant was originally called “The Gatekeeper,” and reflects on the dialogue that made the character so enjoyable to play. He also compares the original game’s performance capture with Hitman 2’s illustrated cutscenes, discusses what he felt was missing from his character’s movement in Hitman 3, and explains why he would have brought more fear and physical discomfort to The Constant’s interrogation.

Beyond his performance, Philip talks about his own love of the series, including why Blood Money is his favorite Hitman game, his memories of Codename 47 and Silent Assassin, and why he preferred exploring missions without maps or hints.

What does the actor behind The Constant think of his character’s biggest scenes? Watch Philip Rosch revisit his performance and share the stories behind Hitman’s calculating villain.

snippet.title: REAL Military Tactics in Ready or Not | Experts React
snippet.description:
What happens when military veterans bring real combat experience into Ready or Not and then break down their own gameplay?

In this Gamology Experts React episode, Damian Hughes and the Advanced Tactics team review their run through Neon Tomb, a challenging nightclub mission where communication, coordination, and split-second decisions can make all the difference.

The team analyzes room clearing, doorway coverage, civilian detentions, rules of engagement, and the balance between moving quickly and taking a more deliberate approach. They explain why preparing before a mission matters, how simple callouts keep everyone coordinated, and why working together consistently can matter more than memorizing complicated tactics.

They also discuss where Ready or Not captures the consequences of real combat and where video games work differently, especially when teammates can communicate freely without nearby enemies hearing them. From protecting civilians to maintaining rear security, one mistake can put the entire squad at risk.

Do real military tactics work in Ready or Not? Watch the team explain what worked, what they could improve, and why they restart a mission when someone gets killed or breaks the rules of engagement.

snippet.title: Pilot Plays Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown | Compilation
snippet.description:
Today on Experts Play we have US Navy Pilot David Gregor in to try out Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown. Having already reacted to Ace Combat 7 last year we thought it only fair for David to return and try out the game for himself and put his skills to the test. Whilst flying David gives an in-depth overview of how realistic the game feels, how the plane handles, and other key details. Be sure to let us know what you thought of today's playthrough?

Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown, like the rest of the Ace Combat series, forgoes a realistic flight model in favor of arcade-like gameplay to make it more accessible to gamers. Furthermore, players can select Novice or Expert control settings; the latter allows them to perform realistic aircraft maneuvers, such as rolls and high-G turns. As with previous entries in the series, most of the aircraft are real-life licenses, although some fictional superplanes are also included.﻿
